tasks.title: Part-time work and professional access
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write an essay summarising and evaluating the key points from both texts in 240–280 words. Use your own words throughout as far as possible, and include your own ideas in your answers.

promptBlocks.label: Text 1
promptBlocks.title: A stepping stone to professional networks
promptBlocks.text: Part-time work is often dismissed as a distraction from academic study, yet it can serve as a crucial entry point into professional networks that full-time education alone rarely provides. For students who lack family connections in desirable industries, a part-time role in a relevant workplace offers exposure to mentors, references and informal knowledge about career progression. The convenience of earning while learning may be the very mechanism that enables access for those who would otherwise be excluded. To restrict part-time work in the name of academic focus is to ignore its role as a leveller in an unequal labour market.

promptBlocks.label: Text 2
promptBlocks.title: The trap of short-term convenience
promptBlocks.text: The argument that part-time work opens doors overlooks the long-term cost of short-term convenience. Students who take on jobs during term time often sacrifice the very activities that build durable professional capital: internships, research projects, volunteering and sustained academic excellence. The networks gained through casual work are typically limited to low-skill sectors and rarely translate into the kind of career advancement that justifies the trade-off. Moreover, the immediate financial benefit can create a dependency that discourages students from pursuing more ambitious but less immediately remunerative opportunities. Convenience today may mean constraint tomorrow.

tasks.title: Review of a part-time work experience programme
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style. A specialist magazine for career advisers is running a series of reviews of part-time work experience programmes aimed at students. You decide to write a review of a programme you have observed or participated in. In your review, describe the programme and its intended purpose, assess how effectively it balances the student's immediate need for income with long-term career development, and recommend whether other institutions should adopt a similar model.

tasks.title: Report on part-time work and academic performance
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style. You are a consultant hired by a university's student welfare office. The programme coordinator has asked you to write a report on how part-time work affects students' academic performance and well-being. In your report, analyse the main tensions between earning income and maintaining academic engagement, assess the potential consequences for student retention and success if these tensions are not addressed, and propose two concrete actions the university could take to support students who work part-time.

tasks.title: Article: Should students take part-time jobs?
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 280–320 words in an appropriate style. An English-language online magazine for international students is publishing a series on 'Work and Study'. You have been contacted by the editor, who asks you to write an article explaining your position on whether university students should take part-time jobs during term time. In your article, discuss what you see as the main advantage and the main disadvantage of part-time work for students, and recommend how students should decide whether to take a job. End your article by requesting that the magazine arrange a follow-up discussion with readers and career advisers to explore the issue further.

designReview.specificSetting: experience and professional access planning brief 8

tasks.scenario: Two source texts debating whether part-time work provides access to professional networks or traps students in low-skill convenience.
tasks.purpose: Synthesise competing claims, evaluate assumptions and develop an independent position on whether part-time work enables or constrains professional access.
requiredContentPoints: part-time work as a stepping stone to professional networks
part-time work as a trap of short-term convenience
own conceptual distinction (e.g., when part-time work is beneficial vs. harmful)
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Source texts use distinct metaphors ('stepping stone' vs. 'trap') and focus on professional access, not generic work-study balance. No overlap with previous C2 tests.

tasks.scenario: Review of a part-time work experience programme for career advisers' magazine.
tasks.purpose: Assess effectiveness of a programme in balancing immediate income with long-term career development, and recommend adoption.
requiredContentPoints: description of the programme and its intended purpose
assessment of balance between income and career development
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Review genre with specific focus on programme design and career impact, not a generic event review. No similar task in existing C2 tests.

tasks.scenario: Report for university student welfare office on part-time work effects on academic performance and well-being.
tasks.purpose: Analyse tensions between earning and academic engagement, assess consequences, and propose actions.
requiredContentPoints: analysis of tensions between income and academic engagement
two concrete actions for the university
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Report focuses on institutional support, not individual advice. No overlap with previous report tasks (e.g., C2-test-01 task 3 was about a jobs fair).

tasks.scenario: Article for international students' magazine on whether to take part-time jobs during term time.
tasks.purpose: Explain position on part-time work, discuss main advantage and disadvantage, recommend decision process, and request follow-up discussion.
requiredContentPoints: main advantage of part-time work for students
main disadvantage of part-time work for students
tasks.originalitySelfCheck: Article ends with a request for follow-up, a novel structural element. No overlap with previous article tasks (e.g., C2-test-01 task 4 was about slow travel).

designReview.overallOriginalityNote: All tasks are built around the specific setting 'experience and professional access planning brief 8' with part-time work as the central theme. No forbidden concepts (e.g., peer learning, language exchange, generic education) are used. Each task has a distinct audience, purpose, and required content points. The source texts in task 1 present opposing views without statistics or named researchers. The review, report, and article tasks require mature evaluation appropriate for C2 level.
